# [Baseline] - WIN - D - Shared Devices Start and Taskbar

Pins Microsoft Edge and Windows App to the taskbar and Start on shared devices, so that every user finds the browser and the remote workplace straight away at the first sign-in.

| | |
|---|---|
| Platform | Windows |
| Scope | Device (D) — assign to device groups |
| Type | Settings Catalog |
| Assignment | — |
| Source | Own baseline — Policy CSP Start/ConfigureStartPins (Windows 11 Start layout) and Start/StartLayout with a CustomTaskbarLayoutCollection (taskbar), Microsoft Learn: Customize the Start layout and Customize the Taskbar on Windows 11. |
| File | [`Baseline_WIN_D_Shared_Devices_Start_and_Taskbar.json`](Baseline_WIN_D_Shared_Devices_Start_and_Taskbar.json) |

> Belongs on SG-D-UEM-WIN-Shared. The taskbar gets Edge and Windows App after the default Windows icons; that happens at the first sign-in of a profile, which on a Shared PC is every new user. Start gets Edge, Windows App, File Explorer and Settings; that replaces the whole list of pinned apps and users cannot change it. Windows App has to be on the device: deploy it as a Store app (9N1F85V9T8BN) via CIPP or Intune, otherwise the spot stays empty. A desktop shortcut cannot be set by policy: Edge creates one itself, Windows App needs a script. Windows 11 only. Check the app ID of Windows App (MicrosoftCorporationII.Windows365_8wekyb3d8bbwe!Windows365) on a device with Get-StartApps.
